hook: SCP-1165 is a document about a place, and nearly all of its tension comes from procedures and percentages rather than from anything happening. The article repeatedly defers what has actually been found inside to a separate Survey Log 1165, which is not part of this page. It reads best as a map with the most interesting parts deliberately held back.
whyItMatters: It is a quiet take on the urban-space anomaly: an ordinary downtown alley that sometimes opens onto an empty duplicate city. There is no monster and no casualty list, only a direction of travel and a probability, and the restraint is the point. The mystery tag is earned by tucking the biggest questions into parenthetical exceptions.
thingsToNotice: The containment section gives away more than the description does. Surveys may not go in at night or when a power cut is possible, and anyone seen coming out is treated as hostile until shown otherwise, yet the description insists that no people or animals have been spotted inside, with the single exception handed off to the survey log. The city itself is a collage: 17% of surveyed buildings match or closely resemble ones in the real town, 24% resemble buildings from elsewhere, an Eiffel Tower lookalike stands on the skyline, and every lamp and traffic light runs with no one maintaining it. The discovery account ends on a politician and his campaign volunteers who walked into the alley at midday and were never found.
